research.text:
**Verdict: SKIP**

**Recommendation:** Do not book flights or travel to White Pass for Saturday. Stay in Denver and save your PTO and travel budget for a colder storm setup. 

### Why This Is Not Worth Pursuing
While Friday offers an impressive 25-inch powder cycle (20 inches opening, 5 inches during the day), you are unable to reach the resort until Saturday. The timing leaves you on the wrong side of a severe Cascade weather transition. 

On Friday night, an atmospheric surge will deliver 0.7 inches of rain from the 4,500-foot base all the way to the 6,500-foot summit. White Pass does not have high-alpine terrain that extends above the forecast freezing line to preserve dry snow. Saturday morning brings an immediate refreeze with virtually no new snow accumulation (1 inch opening, 0 inches during the day). 

The result will be a complete mountainwide freeze: the 25 inches of fresh snow will solidify into a rutted, bulletproof rain crust. For an expert skier seeking fresh powder and tree glades, off-piste skiing in areas like Paradise Basin will be virtually unskiable, hazardous, and jarring. Furthermore, White Pass is not covered on your Ikon Pass (it operates independently on the Indy Pass/Powder Alliance), meaning you would be spending out-of-pocket lift ticket costs on top of flights, car rentals, and lodging for boilerplate conditions.

### What Would Change the Plan
* **Cold Front Acceleration:** If updated model runs show the snow level dropping Friday evening to keep precipitation frozen across the upper mountain (above 5,000–5,500 feet), the upper lifts could preserve skiable snow.
* **Significant Backside Snowfall:** A Saturday morning burst bringing 6 to 10+ inches of dry snow over the refreeze crust would soften turns and open up groomers and milder trees.

Without those drastic shifts, deploying an ~$800 travel budget and PTO days from Denver to intercept a post-rain freeze is a bad value. Look closer to home across the Rockies or wait for a Pacific Northwest storm that stays snow-to-base.
